stem.en: GAAP stands for:

explanation.en: GAAP are the rules and guidelines generally accepted for recording and reporting business transactions.

stem.en: The main purpose of following GAAP is to:

options.en: Bring uniformity and consistency to accounting records and statements
Increase the profit of the business

explanation.en: Uniform rules make financial statements of different firms and years comparable and understandable.

stem.en: Generally accepted accounting principles have evolved:

options.en: Only from the Income Tax Act
By a single order of the Supreme Court
Over a long period, from past experience, usage, customs and statutes

explanation.en: GAAP developed gradually from experience, customs, legal statements and the work of professional bodies.

stem.en: Which term is used in NCERT for the basic assumptions, rules and guidelines on which accounting is based?

explanation.en: GAAP are expressed through basic accounting concepts (also called principles, postulates or conventions).

stem.en: Under which concept is the owner treated as a creditor of the business to the extent of the capital introduced?

explanation.en: The business is a separate entity from its owner, so capital is shown as owed by the business to the owner.

stem.en: Land was bought for ₹10,00,000. Its market value is now ₹15,00,000. In the books it will be shown at ₹10,00,000 because of the:

explanation.en: Under the historical cost concept, assets are recorded at the price paid to acquire them.

stem.en: Depreciation is charged on fixed assets on the assumption that the business will continue for a long time. This follows the:

explanation.en: Because the firm is assumed to run indefinitely, the cost of fixed assets is spread over their useful life.

stem.en: "Every transaction has two aspects, debit and credit, of equal amount" is the:

explanation.en: The dual aspect concept is the basis of the double entry system and the accounting equation.

stem.en: Under the money measurement concept, which of the following will be recorded in the books?

options.en: Good relations of the owner with customers
A strike by workers lasting a week
Appointment of a highly qualified manager

explanation.en: Only events measurable in money are recorded; skill, morale and relations cannot be measured in money.

stem.en: Closing stock costing ₹50,000 has a net realisable value of ₹46,000. It will be valued at:

explanation.en: Under conservatism (prudence) stock is valued at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower.

stem.en: Expenses of a period are set against the revenue of the same period under the:

explanation.en: Matching ensures that profit is measured by comparing revenue with the expenses incurred to earn it.

stem.en: Small items like a stapler or a pencil sharpener are treated as an expense even though they last for years, because of the:

explanation.en: Items too small to affect a user's decision need not be treated in detail; they are written off as expenses.

stem.en: Revenue is recognised when:

options.en: The sale is made and the right to receive payment is established
An order is received from the customer
Cash is received, whichever year the sale was made

explanation.en: Under the revenue recognition (realisation) concept, revenue is recorded when it is earned, not when cash comes in.

stem.en: A firm changes its method of depreciation every year so that profit always looks good. Which concept is violated?

explanation.en: Consistency requires the same accounting methods year after year, so that results can be compared.

stem.en: The system of accounting in which both aspects of every transaction are recorded is the:

explanation.en: The double entry system records the debit and credit aspects of every transaction; it is complete and scientific.

stem.en: Under the cash basis of accounting, entries are made:

options.en: Only when cash is received or paid
Only at the end of the year
When revenue is earned or expense incurred

explanation.en: The cash basis ignores outstanding and accrued items; it records only actual receipts and payments.

stem.en: In 2024-25 a firm made sales of ₹5,00,000 (cash received ₹4,20,000) and incurred expenses of ₹3,10,000 (paid ₹2,90,000). Profit under the accrual basis is:

explanation.en: Accrual basis uses revenue earned and expenses incurred: ₹5,00,000 − ₹3,10,000 = ₹1,90,000.

stem.en: The single entry system is:

options.en: The same as the double entry system
An incomplete and unscientific way of keeping records

explanation.en: Under single entry, only some transactions (mainly cash and personal accounts) are recorded, so it is incomplete.

stem.en: For the same firm (sales ₹5,00,000, cash received ₹4,20,000; expenses ₹3,10,000, paid ₹2,90,000), profit under the cash basis is:

explanation.en: Cash basis: cash received − cash paid = ₹4,20,000 − ₹2,90,000 = ₹1,30,000.

stem.en: In India, the Accounting Standards Board (ASB) was set up in 1977 by the:

options.en: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
Securities and Exchange Board of India

explanation.en: The ICAI constituted the ASB in April 1977 to formulate accounting standards.

stem.en: Accounting standards are:

options.en: Written policy documents on recognition, measurement, treatment, presentation and disclosure of transactions
Laws passed by Parliament for every firm

explanation.en: Accounting standards are written statements issued by an expert body that bring uniformity to financial reporting.

stem.en: IFRS are issued by the:

explanation.en: International Financial Reporting Standards are issued by the IASB, which replaced the IASC in 2001.

stem.en: Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) are:

options.en: Standards that apply only to partnership firms
Standards converged with IFRS and notified by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs
Rules issued by the RBI for banks only
The same as the Income Tax Act

explanation.en: Ind AS are converged with IFRS; they were notified by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs in 2015 for specified companies.

stem.en: On an intra-state sale (within Karnataka) of ₹50,000 at 18% GST, the tax charged will be:

explanation.en: For a sale within a state, GST is split equally: CGST 9% = ₹4,500 and SGST 9% = ₹4,500.

stem.en: On an inter-state sale, the GST levied is:

explanation.en: Integrated GST (IGST) is levied by the Centre on inter-state supplies.

stem.en: GST came into force in India on:

explanation.en: GST was introduced from 1 July 2017, replacing many indirect taxes such as excise duty, VAT and service tax.

stem.en: A dealer paid GST of ₹2,700 on purchases and collected GST of ₹4,500 on sales in a month. Using input tax credit, the net GST payable is:

explanation.en: Input tax credit allows the tax paid on purchases to be set off: ₹4,500 − ₹2,700 = ₹1,800.

stem.en: Which statement about GST is correct?

options.en: It is a direct tax on income
It is collected only by state governments
It is a destination-based tax on consumption

explanation.en: GST is an indirect, destination-based consumption tax on the supply of goods and services.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Closing stock is valued at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower.
Reason (R): The conservatism concept requires that expected profits are not anticipated but all possible losses are provided for.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Valuing stock at the lower figure is a direct application of conservatism, so R correctly explains A.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Under the money measurement concept, the skill of a firm's manager is recorded in the books.
Reason (R): Only transactions that can be expressed in money are recorded in the books of accounts.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: skill cannot be measured in money, so it is not recorded. R correctly states the concept.

stem.en: The GST charged on the sale to Sneha of Mysuru is:

explanation.en: Mysuru is in Karnataka, so it is an intra-state sale: CGST 9% = ₹7,200 and SGST 9% = ₹7,200.

passage.en: Ravi Electronics of Bengaluru (Karnataka) deals in televisions. In June it sold goods worth ₹80,000 to Sneha of Mysuru and goods worth ₹50,000 to Kumar of Chennai (Tamil Nadu). The GST rate on televisions is 18%. During June Ravi Electronics paid GST of ₹12,000 on its purchases.

stem.en: After claiming input tax credit, the net GST payable by Ravi Electronics for June is:

explanation.en: Output GST = ₹14,400 (Mysuru) + ₹9,000 IGST (Chennai) = ₹23,400. Net payable = ₹23,400 − ₹12,000 = ₹11,400.

passage.en: Ravi Electronics of Bengaluru (Karnataka) deals in televisions. In June it sold goods worth ₹80,000 to Sneha of Mysuru and goods worth ₹50,000 to Kumar of Chennai (Tamil Nadu). The GST rate on televisions is 18%. During June Ravi Electronics paid GST of ₹12,000 on its purchases.
